cards.text: The prophet Hosea married Gomer, and the LORD named each of their three kids, with a reason: Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi. Lo-ruhamah, because He would no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, though He would on Judah. Lo-ammi, because He said, 'you are not My people, and I am not your God.'
And right after all that, the very next word is 'Yet.' Friend, that is a BIG little word.

cards.question: Yet what will the number of the Israelites be like?
In the very place they were told 'You are not My people' what will they be called?
Then the promise keeps going. The people of ___ and of ___ will be gathered together.
When Judah and Israel are gathered together, they appoint many leaders for themselves.

cards.text: They'll go up out of the land, and then: 'For great will be the day of Jezreel.' Friend, that's the name of Hosea's first kid, and back in Hosea 1:4 it came with a warning.
Then the LORD Himself speaks, and He's got new words for the brothers and sisters.

cards.question: What does the LORD say the brothers should be called?
And the sisters? What does the LORD say they should be called?

cards.text: From 'not My people' to 'My people.' Friend, I went from a 25-cent sticker in a bakery bin to being called Papa, so I KNOW what a new name does to you.
Then the tone changes. HARD. The LORD says, 'Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not My wife, and I am not her husband.'
Back in Hosea 1:2, the LORD said the land was departing from Him. Here He paints that picture as a wife who's been unfaithful.

cards.question: In this picture, what does the LORD want the wife to remove?

cards.text: And if she won't? The LORD says He'll strip her and expose her, like the day of her birth.

cards.question: If she won't turn, what else does the LORD say He'll make her like?
The LORD says He will have compassion on her children.

cards.text: The reason given: their mother has played the harlot. And she's made up her mind to go after her lovers.

cards.question: Why does the mother say she'll go after her lovers?

answers.text: They give her food and clothes

cards.text: So the LORD says what He'll do. He'll hedge up her path with thorns and wall her in.

cards.question: Why does the LORD hedge up her path with thorns and a wall?

answers.text: So she can't find her way
So her lovers can find her
So she can build a home

cards.text: Every road she tries? ROAD CLOSED. Detour. ROAD CLOSED. Friend, that's your worst Monday commute, all day long.

cards.question: She chases after her lovers anyway. What happens?
When she can't find her lovers, what does she decide?

answers.text: To return to her first husband
To stay alone in the desert

cards.text: And she says it herself: 'for then I was better off than now.' I said a line like that every day in the back of a junk drawer, missing my old spot on the counter.
But here's the part that stings. The LORD says she doesn't acknowledge where her grain, new wine and oil really came from.

cards.question: She credits her lovers, but it was the ___ who gave her grain, new wine and oil.

cards.text: That's me, my first week on the Millers' counter, thanking the timer for the cookies. The timer didn't bake ANYTHING, friend. It just beeped.
It gets worse. The silver and gold He lavished on her? They crafted it for Baal, a false god.

cards.question: So what does the LORD say He'll do with His grain and new wine?
The LORD says the wool and linen He gave her were meant to cover her.
The LORD says He'll expose her in front of her lovers. Who can deliver her out of His hands?
The LORD says He'll put an end to all her exultation. What does that include?

cards.text: Next come her vines and fig trees. The LORD says He'll destroy them, turn them into a thicket, and let the beasts of the field devour them.

cards.question: She thinks those vines and fig trees are wages. Who does she think paid them?

cards.text: Then the LORD names the days of the Baals, when she burned incense to them, put on rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers.

cards.question: After that whole list, what does the LORD say she did to Him?

cards.text: 'But Me she forgot,' declares the LORD. Friend, I know what being forgotten in the dark feels like, and hearing the LORD Himself say it? That one lands heavy.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. ... If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Card 13 says this is 'a wife who's been unfaithful' right before card 14 asks what she should remove. That gives away the answer 'Her adultery and unfaithfulness' and rules out the wrong answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The statement 'The LORD says He will have compassion on her children' has no context. It doesn't say who 'her' is, and it doesn't say this is part of the warning if she won't turn. The passage also says the sisters will be called 'My loved one' (Hosea 2:1), so a baker could argue 'True' from elsewhere in the passage.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question asks why the mother 'say[s]' she'll go after her lovers, but Hosea 2:5 says 'she thought.' Card 18 also changes 'she thought' into 'she's made up her mind.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

Card 6 does something similar by saying he 'said a line like that every day' in the drawer, even though the backstory says he didn't talk much there.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: This two-blank fill in the blank has right answers that can swap places: 'Judah' and 'Israel.' A baker who puts Israel in blank 1 and Judah in blank 2 has the meaning right but would be marked wrong.
findings.question: When two blanks can swap without changing the meaning, should both orders count as right, or should cards like this be avoided?
